EWDOC files (Egyptian Writer Document) are this app\'s native files. They contain the MdC code, its GlyphX representation and the properties. The MdC and GlyphX code encodes the hieroglyphs, while the properties explain how to display the signs.
Because the format doesn\'t include image data, the files are very small and you can edit the hieroglyphic text easily.
However, this file format is only supported by the Egyptian Writer App.
Recommended for: sharing hieroglyphic texts between users of this app and building backups of the documents

SVG files (Scalable Vector Graphic) are images that are described by mathematical formulas rather than pixels.
This means they can easily be used in programs like Inkscape, do not become pixelated when zoomed in, and require less disk space than to other image formats.
However, please note that SVG files are not supported everywhere, and they do not contain hieroglyphic text. This means that you can only view the text and edit the signs, not the text itself.
Recommended for: art, web applications, big posters and for importing into office programs such as LibreOffice or MS Word
Read more: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SVG

PNG files (Portable Network Graphic), unlike SVG files, save their content as pixels. Each pixel has a colour value. Together with other pixels, they shape the image. Although PNG files are lossless compressed, they still require much more disk space than SVG files and become pixelated very quickly, when zoomed in.
However, PNG files are supported by nearly every program and also contain an alpha channel, which allows you to make the background transparent.
Please note that, like every other image format, PNG files do not contain hieroglyphic text. This means that it is impossible to change the text content after exporting.
Recommended for: sharing via messengers or email, printing, and for including in PDF documents
Read more: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PNG

JPEG files (Joint Photographic Experts Group), like PNG files, save their content as pixels. Each pixel has a colour value. Together with other pixels, they shape the image. Unlike PNG files, JPEG files are compressed lossily. This results in lower quality, but also smaller file sizes.
Nevertheless, JPEG files still require much more disk space than SVG files and become pixelated very quickly, when zoomed in.
They also do not have an alpha channel, meaning the background cannot be transparent. However, JPEG files are supported by nearly every program and, because of their smaller file size, are suitable for sending via email.
Please note that, like every other image format, JPEG files do not contain hieroglyphic text. This means that it is impossible to change the text content after exporting.
Recommended for: sharing via messengers or email
Read more: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JPEG
